findings.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId is doubly broken: it returns false exactly when the grant shortcut EQUALS the expected value (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), and it reads substring(3,5) — the tokenType char plus the first grant char — instead of the grant shortcut at substring(4,6) of the 6-char context. The grant assertions added to expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken and expectAuthReqIdToToken are inert: any encoded token id with a UUID tail matches regardless of grant type, so a regression that encodes the wrong grant shortcut into access token ids passes the whole integration suite undetected; conversely anyone who fixes only the inverted comparison makes substring(3,5) (values like 'ta','tc','tr') never equal the expected shortcut, failing every currently-correct token, and a short prefix such as ':1234' throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException inside the matcher instead of returning false.

[BUG] The constructor's fourth guard is a copy-paste of the third — Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") checks grantType again instead of rawTokenId, so the rawTokenId null guard is dead code. A caller constructing AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId gets no fail-fast; encodeTokenId then string-concatenates it, minting a jti ending in the literal 'null' (e.g. 'onrtcc:null') that round-trips through getTokenContextFromTokenId as the string "null", silently corrupting the token id the framework exists to protect.

[BUG] testIncorrectGrantType passes via a NullPointerException, not the IllegalArgumentException it claims to verify: before() calls only factory.init(null) (postInit is never invoked, so the sessionFactory field stays null), and getGrantTypeByShortcut('ac') dereferences sessionFactory on the map miss, with the broad catch(RuntimeException) swallowing the NPE. Deleting the 'Unknown value ... for grant type' IllegalArgumentException throw in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId keeps this test green (the AccessTokenContext requireNonNull NPE would also satisfy the catch), so the malformed-token-id contract the encoder promises has zero verification.

[ADVISORY] getShortcut() is added to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory as an abstract method with no default implementation, making every existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory binary-incompatible. An operator upgrading Keycloak with a custom grant extension jar installed hits AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls getShortcut() on the old-compiled factory during startup — the server fails to boot entirely, with no feature flag or fallback to disable the new token-id encoding without patching the extension.

[ADVISORY] postInit feeds every grant factory's getShortcut() straight into ConcurrentHashMap.put, so a third-party factory returning null (the interface contract only says 'should be unique', never non-null) crashes with a bare NullPointerException, and any shortcut collision aborts the entire server boot via IllegalStateException. Operators deploying any custom grant whose shortcut is null or duplicates an in-tree one (e.g. an extension picking 'cc') get an opaque NPE stack trace or a bricked startup rather than a disabled grant — the failure mode for any shortcut-related extension problem is total boot failure, inconsistent with the diagnosable duplicate-check message the author clearly intended.

[ADVISORY] The public copy constructor Context(Context) is deleted while the mutators it served (setFormParams, setClient) are retained, breaking source and binary compatibility for third-party grant implementations that used the copy-then-mutate pattern this SPI exists to support. Custom grant extensions compiled against the previous interface throw NoSuchMethodError the first time the grant handles a token request, turning every request to that grant into a 500, and extension source builds referencing the constructor stop compiling — nothing in this change requires the removal.

[ADVISORY] The 'Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' branches in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut are unreachable in production because Keycloak registers provider factories only at startup, before postInit populates the maps, so no grant can appear later. The dead branches add the sessionFactory dereference that the unit test trips as an NPE (see testIncorrectGrantType) and mislead maintainers into believing grants hot-deploy; deleting them removes ~15 lines, the null-sessionFactory trap, and the only reads of the sessionFactory field outside postInit, making the field itself deletable.

[BUG] AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId reads items[0].substring(3, 5) — the 4th and 5th chars, i.e. the last char of the tokenType plus the first char of the grant shortcut — instead of the 5th-6th chars where the grant shortcut actually lives, and inverts the comparison by returning false when the substring equals the expected grant, so the grant assertion never rejects anything. All four updated matchers (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) reduce to a bare 'prefix:UUID' shape check — with the current enum shortcuts the early return can never fire — so a regression that encodes the wrong grant type or no grant type into issued token IDs ships with a fully green testsuite; the diff's only integration-level verification of grant encoding is vacuous.

[BUG] Constants.GRANT_TYPE is set only in exchangeClientToOIDCClient, leaving the sibling token-minting paths in the same class — exchangeOIDCtoOIDC and exchangeSAMLtoOIDC, the standard token-exchange flows where the subject token is an OIDC or SAML token — building their ClientSessionContext without the attribute. Access tokens minted on the primary token-exchange path encode grant context 'na' instead of 'te', so the TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory shortcut registered in this diff is unreachable for real exchanges and any consumer of the encoded context misclassifies every exchanged token; no test or matcher in the diff asserts the exchange grant, so nothing detects it.

[BUG] The getShortcut() contract tells implementers the shortcut is 'usually like 3-letters' and requires only uniqueness, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-requires a 6-char prefix (exactly 2-char shortcuts) and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit validates neither shortcut length nor null. A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory following the Javadoc with a 3-char shortcut mints tokens whose IDs the same server's decoder rejects with IllegalArgumentException ('Expected length of 6'), and a factory returning null from getShortcut() crashes Keycloak startup with a bare NullPointerException from ConcurrentHashMap.put in postInit with no hint at the offending factory.

[ADVISORY] The constructor's fourth guard is a copy-paste of the third — Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") checks grantType a second time — so the rawTokenId null-check its error message promises does not exist. A null rawTokenId is accepted and encodeTokenId then silently emits a token ID ending in the literal string ':null'; the fail-fast invariant the guard claims to enforce is absent for exactly the field named in the message, so the next caller that trusts the constructor's validation gets corrupt token IDs instead of an exception.

[ADVISORY] The only test in the diff never invokes getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext or postInit — before() hand-assigns the package-private grants maps instead of driving the factory's real initialization — and the integration matcher isAccessTokenId verifies only the prefix:UUID split, leaving prefix positions 0-4 unasserted. The classification logic executed for every issued token (online/offline/transient, lightweight/regular) and the production grant-registry construction (the duplicate-shortcut validation and the UNKNOWN self-mapping) have zero coverage: a regression swapping OFFLINE with ONLINE, or dropping the UNKNOWN mapping in postInit so encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException for every token minted on an unattributed path, ships with a green build.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId degrades pre-framework IDs (no colon) to UNKNOWN but throws IllegalArgumentException for any 6-char prefix containing an unregistered shortcut, the prefix carries no version marker, and no production code in this diff calls the decode half at all. When the consumer this framework is built for is wired up, a token minted while a custom grant was deployed becomes hard-undecodable after that grant is removed — failing with an exception where old-format tokens degrade gracefully to UNKNOWN — and any future extension of the context format breaks decoding of all in-flight tokens the same way; the entire asymmetry ships unexercised.

[ADVISORY] The tokenType component is derived from session.getContext().getClient() via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session) instead of the client parameter initToken already holds. On the token-exchange paths this same diff touches, where the token is minted for a target client different from the authenticated session-context client, the encoded lt/rt marker tracks the requesting client's lightweight-access-token configuration and can contradict the actual shape of the issued token.

[BUG] The isAccessTokenId matcher both slices the wrong characters (substring(3,5) instead of the grant shortcut's actual position substring(4,6)) and inverts its condition (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns no-match when the grant matches), so it accepts any '<6-char-prefix>:<uuid>' token ID regardless of grant type. expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh and expectAuthReqidToToken never actually verify the encoded grant shortcut — CI stays green even if TokenManager stamps the wrong grant into every token ID, leaving this PR's headline behavior with zero effective integration verification.

[BUG] Only exchangeClientToOIDCClient sets the Constants.GRANT_TYPE client-session attribute; the provider's other exchange flows (e.g. exchangeOIDCtoOIDC user token exchange) issue access tokens through TokenManager.responseBuilder without ever setting the attribute, so those tokens encode the 'na' unknown-grant shortcut instead of 'te'. Standard user token exchange — a first-class grant with a registered 'te' shortcut — silently violates the framework's core invariant that every access token records its grant type, so any consumer of the encoded context misclassifies exchanged tokens and the TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory shortcut is never emitted.

[BUG] getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-requires a 6-character context prefix (length != 6 throws IllegalArgumentException, grant read via substring(4,6)), but the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory contract it relies on documents shortcuts as 'usually like 3-letters' with only uniqueness required, and postInit never validates shortcut length or charset. A third-party grant factory returning a 3-character (or colon-containing) shortcut registers cleanly and its tokens encode fine, but every such token ID then fails decode with IllegalArgumentException — the framework cannot round-trip output produced under its own documented SPI contract.

[BUG] The constructor's rawTokenId guard checks grantType a second time — Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") — so rawTokenId is never null-checked despite the guard's message. A null rawTokenId is accepted and encodeTokenId silently emits '<prefix>:null', which decodes back as the literal string "null" as the token's raw ID instead of failing fast as the guard intends.

[BUG] The lazy 'Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' paths in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut insert into the shared grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts maps on miss without any duplicate-shortcut check, bypassing the uniqueness validation postInit enforces at boot. A grant deployed after startup whose shortcut collides with an existing one silently overwrites the mapping — e.g. a late 'cc' grant shadows client-credentials — so token IDs already in circulation decode to the wrong grant type with no error anywhere; the invariant postInit claims to guarantee is not enforced on the exact path the code anticipates.

[ADVISORY] initToken unconditionally routes every access token ID through the new encoder — changing the jti/ID wire format from a bare UUID to '<6-char-context>:<uuid>' with no feature flag or config switch — while getTokenContextFromTokenId, the only API that reads the encoded context back, has zero production call sites in this diff. Every consumer that treats token IDs as UUIDs (audit pipelines, DB column constraints, external dedup logic — and this diff's own testsuite, which needed four matcher rewrites) breaks now, and the breakage purchases no in-release behavior since nothing in Keycloak reads the context back; an operator needing the old format has no rollback short of a code change.

[ADVISORY] getShortcut() is added to the public OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI interface as an abstract method with no default implementation, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit invokes it on every registered grant factory during KeycloakSessionFactory initialization. An out-of-tree grant factory compiled against the previous SPI throws AbstractMethodError inside postInit (or, if its getShortcut() returns null, a bare NullPointerException from ConcurrentHashMap.put(null, ...)), aborting startup — deployments with custom OAuth2 grant types, a common extension point, cannot boot after upgrade; a default method returning 'na' would have preserved them.

[ADVISORY] The public Context(Context) copy constructor is deleted outright rather than extended to copy the new grantType field. Out-of-tree OAuth2GrantType implementations that call new Context(otherContext) fail with NoSuchMethodError at runtime after upgrade — a binary break not traceable to the encoding feature, which only required the copy to carry grantType.

[ADVISORY] grantType is derived once at construction via formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE), but the public setFormParams mutator does not re-derive it, and the constructor now NPEs on a null formParams the previous code tolerated. A grant implementation that constructs Context and then replaces the form params via setFormParams (the mutator exists for exactly that) mints tokens stamped with the stale construction-time grant — or crashes at construction where the old code accepted null — encoding the wrong grant shortcut into every token it issues.

[ADVISORY] The test setup never runs postInit — it calls init(null) and hand-assigns the package-private maps — leaving the factory's sessionFactory null, so testIncorrectGrantType passes by catching a NullPointerException from the lazy-refresh path rather than the intended IllegalArgumentException. The unknown-grant-type rejection behavior is verified only by accident (an NPE happens to be a RuntimeException), and the production initialization path — postInit's duplicate-shortcut detection and UNKNOWN seeding — has no test at all, so regressions there pass CI.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the only method the production token-issuance path actually calls — is exercised by no test: the unit test covers only decode/encode round-trips over hand-built maps, and the AssertEvents matcher checks neither session type nor token type. A regression in session-type derivation (e.g. swapping the OFFLINE and ONLINE branches), lightweight-token detection, or the null-grant-to-UNKNOWN fallback ships silently — every test in this diff stays green while every issued token carries the wrong context.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId's grant check is dead code twice over: it slices items[0].substring(3, 5), which is the tokenType's second char plus the grant's first char (the grant shortcut lives at substring(4, 6) of the 2+2+2 prefix), and the equality is inverted (it returns false when the slice equals the expected shortcut), so the grant type is never actually verified. expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh and expectAuthReqIdToToken all pass for any 'xxxxxx:uuid' token id regardless of grant — including 'onrtna:uuid' tokens issued by a path that forgot to set Constants.GRANT_TYPE — so the testsuite stays green while the grant-encoding property it claims to assert is absent, and the production grant-shortcut wiring is validated nowhere.

[BUG] The constructor's null guard for rawTokenId checks grantType a second time (Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")), so rawTokenId is never validated. A null rawTokenId is silently accepted and encodeTokenId then emits the literal string 'null' into the token id ('onrtna:null'), producing an id that fails every isUUID-based check and cannot be decoded back to a real id; the invariant the constructor's error message promises is not enforced.

[BUG] encodeTokenId concatenates the grant shortcut with no length validation while getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-requires the encoded context to be exactly 6 chars (2 per component), and the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() javadoc tells extension authors to use a '3-letters shortcut' — so the writer and reader of the same framework disagree on the canonical form. A custom grant whose factory follows the published javadoc (or returns any shortcut != 2 chars) encodes successfully, but every such token id is then rejected by getTokenContextFromTokenId with IllegalArgumentException ('Expected length of 6'), so the deployment's own freshly issued tokens are undecodable by its own decoder.

[ADVISORY] initToken unconditionally replaces every access token's jti with a 43-char 'xxxxxx:uuid' prefixed value (previously a 36-char UUID), with no feature flag or configuration and with the only override hook (TokenContextEncoderSpi) declared internal. Downstream consumers that stored or validated jti/Details.TOKEN_ID as a UUID — DB columns typed uuid/char(36), event sinks and audit systems correlating by TOKEN_ID — break on upgrade with no opt-out, and every access token now discloses session-persistence state (online/offline/transient) and grant type to every resource server that receives it.

[ADVISORY] The GRANT_TYPE client-session attribute is populated by five hand-maintained call sites using three different mechanisms (form-param via createTokenResponse here, a hardcoded constant in TokenManager.validateToken, and explicit constants in ROPC, pre-authorized-code and token-exchange) instead of one central dispatch point, so any issuance path that misses the setAttribute silently encodes grant 'na'. The next grant added — or any custom OAuth2GrantType that builds its response without OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse — issues tokens with grant 'na' and nothing detects it: the integration matcher's grant check is dead and no production code reads the value yet, so the wrong encoding ships invisibly until a consumer relies on it.

[ADVISORY] Constants.GRANT_TYPE is set only in exchangeClientToOIDCClient; the sibling identity-broker exchange path (ExternalToInternalTokenExchangeProvider) issues access tokens through TokenManager without setting the attribute. Tokens minted via external-IdP-to-internal token exchange encode grant 'na' instead of 'te', so any later consumer of the encoded grant type misclassifies all brokered-exchange tokens.

[ADVISORY] postInit puts gtf.getShortcut() into a ConcurrentHashMap without a null check, and the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface documents no null contract for getShortcut(). A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory whose getShortcut() returns null — a legal implementation of the documented contract — makes ConcurrentHashMap.put(null, ...) throw NullPointerException during postInit, and the whole Keycloak server fails to start with an NPE pointing into the encoder factory rather than a message naming the offending grant.

[ADVISORY] Adding the abstract getShortcut() method to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory with no default implementation, and removing OAuth2GrantType.Context's copy constructor, breaks every out-of-tree grant implementation at compile time. Custom grant-type extensions — the extension point this very framework encodes into tokens — stop compiling against this version until each factory adds getShortcut(), and code using new Context(otherContext) no longer compiles; a minimal port that returns null then bricks startup via the postInit NPE.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId has no production caller in this diff — the encoding is written into every issued access token but read only by the unit test, so the strict 6-char format contract is frozen into long-lived tokens before any production reader exists. When the follow-up consumer PR arrives, any adjustment to the format (a new component, changed widths) makes every token already issued by this version hit the strict decoder and throw IllegalArgumentException, and nothing in production currently exercises the decode path to reveal such drift before tokens are in the wild.

[ADVISORY] The only test of the codec hand-wires the factory's grant maps (three entries assigned directly to package-private fields) instead of exercising postInit's production factory scan, and getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the code that derives sessionType/tokenType for every real token — has no test at all. A wrong shortcut constant in any grant factory, or a postInit wiring mistake that does not throw, ships with an all-green build: the unit test never reads the real factories, the integration matcher's grant check is dead, and the first signal is production tokens carrying wrong context.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId returns false when the extracted grant shortcut EQUALS the expected shortcut, and it extracts the shortcut with substring(3, 5) instead of the correct substring(4, 6) for the 2+2+2 encoding, so the grant-shortcut assertion is both inverted and mis-indexed. All four helpers updated in this diff (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) pass for any token ID of the form '<6+ chars>:<uuid>' regardless of which grant type was encoded — a regression that stamps the wrong grant shortcut into every jti ships silently, and if the equality branch is ever reached it rejects CORRECT token IDs, failing every happy-path test.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice (lines 70 and 71), so the guard whose message promises 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' validates grantType and a null rawTokenId is silently accepted. The documented invariant is unenforced: a caller passing a null rawTokenId gets a context that encodeTokenId renders into a token jti ending in ':null' instead of the promised rejection, and the next reader of the guard believes null is impossible.

[BUG] testIncorrectGrantType passes because getGrantTypeByShortcut throws NullPointerException — sessionFactory is null since postInit is never called and the lazy-refresh branch dereferences it — and the catch (RuntimeException) swallows that unrelated crash instead of the IllegalArgumentException the test intends to exercise. The malformed-token-ID error path of getTokenContextFromTokenId is untested: replacing the intended IllegalArgumentException with an NPE in production code goes unnoticed, and the test green-lights the exact null-sessionFactory crash the half-initialized factory produces.

[ADVISORY] initToken wires the default encoder unconditionally, so the PR's stated objective — a pluggable framework that 'provides ability to encode' context — silently became a mandatory change of the public jti / Details.TOKEN_ID format from a UUID to a positional code like 'onrtac:<uuid>' for every access token in every realm, with no configuration entry to opt out. On upgrade, every OAuth client and every event-log/monitoring pipeline that treats token IDs as UUIDs (dedup keys, typed DB columns, parsers) breaks, and the only escape is deploying a custom TokenContextEncoderProvider jar; the diff itself demonstrates the ripple by being forced to rewrite AssertEvents' TOKEN_ID matchers.

[ADVISORY] getShortcut() is added to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI as an abstract method with no default implementation, while DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls it on every registered grant factory during KeycloakSessionFactory creation. A custom grant jar compiled before this change lacks getShortcut(), so postInit throws AbstractMethodError at startup and the server fails to boot — existing custom-grant deployments hard-fail on upgrade instead of degrading, where a default method (e.g., deriving from getId()) would have preserved compatibility.

[ADVISORY] The getShortcut() javadoc tells implementors to return a 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but the default encoder hard-requires exactly 2 characters (encodedContext.length() != 6 throws IllegalArgumentException) and nothing validates shortcut length at startup or at encode time. A custom grant that follows the documented contract issues access tokens whose IDs the only built-in decoder rejects with 'Expected length of 6' — the published SPI contract and its sole consumer are incompatible, and the mismatch surfaces only as decode failures on production tokens rather than at deployment.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId — the retrieval half of the framework whose javadoc states the purpose as 'this information can be later retrieved from the token' — has no production caller anywhere in this diff; the encoded context is written into every access token's jti but nothing in Keycloak reads it back. The stated objective is only half-delivered: every token carries 7 extra characters that no in-tree code consumes, so the public format change lands with zero offsetting capability unless an unblocked follow-up consumer arrives; if that follow-up is dropped, the format break is permanent with no payoff.

[ADVISORY] The public Context(Context) copy constructor is deleted from the OAuth2GrantType.Context SPI class as part of this change. Any out-of-tree custom grant that forked a Context via the copy constructor no longer compiles against this version — a source-incompatible removal of a public SPI symbol bundled inside a change framed as an 'encoding framework', with no deprecation step.

[ADVISORY] Grant-shortcut uniqueness is enforced only by a map-size comparison that throws IllegalStateException during postInit, with no config-level override to rename a shortcut and no per-factory error identifying the colliding grants. An operator deploying two independently developed custom grant jars that picked the same natural 2-letter code gets a server-wide boot failure with the cryptic message 'Different lengths of maps', fixable only by code changes in one vendor's jar — an outage triggered by a cosmetic identifier.

[ADVISORY] Constants.GRANT_TYPE is set only in exchangeClientToOIDCClient, leaving the provider's other token-minting exchange path (external-token-to-internal exchange) without the attribute. Access tokens minted by external-to-internal exchange are labeled with the UNKNOWN grant code 'na' although they were issued through the token-exchange grant, so any consumer of the encoded grant info receives wrong data for exactly the tokens the sibling path in the same provider labels 'te'.

[ADVISORY] The 'Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' branches in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut are dead code: Keycloak's provider registry is fixed at startup, so every grant type reachable at token-creation time was already iterated in postInit and the lazy lookups can never find anything new. The next maintainer must reason about a hot-deployment mechanism that does not exist and keep the maps mutable plus the sessionFactory field solely for it — this dead path is exactly what the unit test trips into as an NPE; deleting both branches (~15 lines) also removes the sessionFactory null-hazard and lets the maps be immutable like the session/token-type maps.

[ADVISORY] initToken now embeds the session-persistence state, token type, and the OAuth grant type in plaintext in the access-token jti (e.g. an id of 'ofrtro:<uuid>' discloses to any reader an offline session issued via the resource-owner-password grant), where the jti was previously an opaque UUID. Every party that ever holds the access token — any resource server, any audience reached through token exchange, API gateways, and any log or proxy that captures the jti — can decode how the user authenticated and that they hold a long-lived offline session, information previously absent from standard claims; and because DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.init ignores its Config.Scope there is no realm, client, or deployment switch to disable the encoding without shipping a custom provider.

[BUG] The constructor's fourth null guard re-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId — Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") — so rawTokenId is never validated. A context built with a null rawTokenId passes construction instead of failing fast as the guard intends, and encodeTokenId then emits the literal jti '<context>:null', so every token issued through that path shares one jti and resource servers doing jti-based replay detection reject legitimate tokens as replays.

[ADVISORY] The lazy refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut insert into grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts without any duplicate-shortcut check, bypassing the collision validation that postInit enforces, so a grant registered after startup with a shortcut colliding with an existing grant silently overwrites the shortcut-to-grant mapping. In exactly the scenario these methods were written for (the code comment 'Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed'), tokens issued before the redeploy decode via getTokenContextFromTokenId to the wrong grant type with no error raised, feeding misclassified token context to any consumer of the new SPI.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId is doubly broken — it reads the wrong window (items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6), mixing the last char of tokenType with the first char of grantType) and inverts the comparison (returns false when the window EQUALS the expected shortcut) — so it matches any '<6-char-context>:<uuid>' token ID regardless of which grant shortcut was encoded. expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh and expectAuthReqIdToToken pass for any grant: a refresh token whose Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute is dropped (encoding 'na') or a code-to-token response encoding 'cc' still matches, so the only integration-level verification of this PR's grant-encoding feature checks nothing beyond 'one colon plus UUID tail', and regressions in TokenManager.validateToken's refresh wiring or any grant's setAttribute call stay green.

[BUG] testIncorrectGrantType passes by catching a NullPointerException thrown from the null sessionFactory inside DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut's refresh fallback (before() never calls postInit, so sessionFactory is null and 'ac' is absent from the hand-built map), never reaching the IllegalArgumentException('Unknown value ... for grant type') branch the test claims to verify. The unknown-grant-shortcut validation in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId has zero real coverage: because the catch is the broad 'catch (RuntimeException)', deleting the IllegalArgumentException throw entirely leaves this test green, so malformed grant shortcuts in token IDs are unguarded by the suite.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the method TokenManager.initToken calls to derive every issued access-token ID — is never invoked by any test in this diff (checked DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java, whose five methods only exercise getTokenContextFromTokenId/encodeTokenId string round-trips, and AssertEvents.java, whose isAccessTokenId matcher checks only shape). The TRANSIENT/OFFLINE/ONLINE derivation and the lightweight-token detection are unverified: inverting userSession.isOffline() or the persistence-state comparison puts a wrong 'on'/'of'/'tr' prefix on every token issued by the realm and every test in this diff stays green.

[ADVISORY] before() hand-populates the package-private grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts maps with two synthetic entries and never calls factory.postInit, so postInit's provider-registry wiring and its duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException guard are executed by no test. A swapped put() in postInit or a broken duplicate-shortcut guard fails no unit test, and none of the real factory shortcuts ('ac','cc','pg','pc','rt','te','ci','dg','ro') is ever asserted against a real factory — two grants shipping the same shortcut would silently overwrite grantsByShortcuts and corrupt token-ID decoding with the suite green until the untested startup check fires.

[ADVISORY] The decode-side validation branches — the encodedContext.length() != 6 guard and the unknown session-type and token-type shortcut guards — are triggered by no test in the diff (all five test methods feed valid 6-char contexts or the colon-less '1234'). Removing the length guard makes a malformed ID like 'onrtacc:uuid' silently decode with a shifted parse (st='on', tt='rt', gt='ac') instead of throwing, and no test fails; the only negative-path test (testIncorrectGrantType) targets the grant guard and passes via NPE, so none of these three guards has any coverage.

[ADVISORY] encodeTokenId's UNKNOWN-tokenType guard and unknown-grantType guard are never executed: testOldToken's context trips the sessionType guard first (line 101) and every other test encodes known values, so lines 104-106 and 108-111 have zero coverage. Deleting either guard fails no test; an UNKNOWN-tokenType context would then encode as a 'un'-prefixed ID that round-trips back as UNKNOWN without error, silently changing the reject-unknown contract with no suite coverage.

[ADVISORY] The GRANT_TYPE attribute wiring added here and at the grant-specific sites (ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient) has no asserting coverage in this diff's test changes, which reference only the ac/dg/rt/ci shortcuts through the vacuous isAccessTokenId matcher. If createTokenResponse's setAttribute is dropped or a factory's shortcut is mis-registered, client-credentials, password, token-exchange and pre-authorized-code tokens encode 'na' or a wrong shortcut and every test in the diff stays green — the round-trip unit tests use synthetic map entries, not the real factories' shortcuts, so no test ties these grants' wiring to an issued jti.

[BUG] The new isAccessTokenId matcher never validates the grant shortcut: it slices items[0].substring(3, 5) — the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant shortcut — instead of the grant shortcut at substring(4, 6), and its early-return condition is inverted (it returns false when the slice EQUALS the expected shortcut), so the grant check is dead code. The matcher accepts any '<prefix>:<uuid>' token ID regardless of which grant/session/token type was encoded, so the four updated assertions (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) are vacuous — a regression encoding the wrong grant shortcut in every access-token ID passes the integration suite undetected.

[BUG] The AccessTokenContext constructor null-checks grantType twice — the guard labeled "Null rawTokenId not allowed" also calls requireNonNull(grantType, ...), so rawTokenId is never validated despite the message. A caller passing a null rawTokenId (an extension implementing TokenContextEncoderProvider, or a decode-then-re-encode path) does not fail fast but silently produces a token ID containing the literal string 'null' (e.g. 'onrtna:null'), corrupting the jti of every token issued through that path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Grant-shortcut uniqueness is enforced only by a map-size comparison that throws IllegalStateException during postInit, with no config-level override to rename a shortcut and no per-factory error identifying the colliding grants. An operator deploying two independently developed custom grant jars that picked the same natural 2-letter code gets a server-wide boot failure with the cryptic message 'Different lengths of maps', fixable only by code changes in one vendor's jar — an outage triggered by a cosmetic identifier.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), grant shortcuts are collected into two maps (grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts) and uniqueness is validated only by comparing map sizes, throwing IllegalStateException with the generic message "Different lengths of maps..." if a duplicate ID/shortcut exists. The diff shows no code to identify which shortcuts/grants collided and no configuration/override mechanism to resolve collisions at runtime. While duplicate shortcuts must be prevented for correct token-id encoding/decoding, the failure mode and diagnostics are indeed coarse and can cause startup failure when two custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations choose the same shortcut.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Constants.GRANT_TYPE is set only in exchangeClientToOIDCClient, leaving the provider's other token-minting exchange path (external-token-to-internal exchange) without the attribute. Access tokens minted by external-to-internal exchange are labeled with the UNKNOWN grant code 'na' although they were issued through the token-exchange grant, so any consumer of the encoded grant info receives wrong data for exactly the tokens the sibling path in the same provider labels 'te'.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient now sets clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE). The finding claims there is a separate “external-token-to-internal” exchange path in the same provider that mints tokens without setting this attribute, causing UNKNOWN ('na') grant codes. However, no such method/path is shown in the provided diff, so the asserted omission and resulting behavior cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' branches in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut are dead code: Keycloak's provider registry is fixed at startup, so every grant type reachable at token-creation time was already iterated in postInit and the lazy lookups can never find anything new. The next maintainer must reason about a hot-deployment mechanism that does not exist and keep the maps mutable plus the sessionFactory field solely for it — this dead path is exactly what the unit test trips into as an NPE; deleting both branches (~15 lines) also removes the sessionFactory null-hazard and lets the maps be immutable like the session/token-type maps.

adjudication.rationale: The claim that these branches are definitively “dead code” because Keycloak can’t ever add grant providers after startup is not verifiable from the diff alone. However, the diff *does* show that the “refresh maps” branches in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory#getShortcutByGrantType` and `#getGrantTypeByShortcut` introduce extra mutability and a `sessionFactory` dependency, and they can throw an NPE when `sessionFactory` is not initialized (e.g., the new unit test constructs the factory without calling `postInit`, so `getGrantTypeByShortcut` will dereference `sessionFactory` on an unknown shortcut). This is a concrete maintainability/robustness concern grounded in the added code, even if it may not manifest in normal runtime lifecycle.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] initToken now embeds the session-persistence state, token type, and the OAuth grant type in plaintext in the access-token jti (e.g. an id of 'ofrtro:<uuid>' discloses to any reader an offline session issued via the resource-owner-password grant), where the jti was previously an opaque UUID. Every party that ever holds the access token — any resource server, any audience reached through token exchange, API gateways, and any log or proxy that captures the jti — can decode how the user authenticated and that they hold a long-lived offline session, information previously absent from standard claims; and because DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.init ignores its Config.Scope there is no realm, client, or deployment switch to disable the encoding without shipping a custom provider.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes access-token `jti` from an opaque UUID to an encoded string containing contextual metadata. In `TokenManager.initToken`, `token.id(...)` now calls `TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)`, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` constructs `sessionTypeShortcut + tokenTypeShortcut + grantShortcut + ':' + rawTokenId` (e.g. `ofrtro:<uuid>`). `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` derives `SessionType` from `UserSessionModel` (offline/online/transient), `TokenType` from `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)`, and `grantType` from `clientSessionContext.getAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...)`, which is set in multiple flows (`OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`, `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType`, `TokenManager.validateToken` refresh path, `StandardTokenExchangeProvider`, etc.). This makes grant type and session/offline-ness observable to any party that can read/log the token `jti`, which is a concrete information-disclosure change introduced by the diff. Also, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.init(Config.Scope config)` ignores `config`, so the default behavior is not configurable via scope in this implementation (only by swapping providers).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor's fourth null guard re-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId — Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") — so rawTokenId is never validated. A context built with a null rawTokenId passes construction instead of failing fast as the guard intends, and encodeTokenId then emits the literal jti '<context>:null', so every token issued through that path shares one jti and resource servers doing jti-based replay detection reject legitimate tokens as replays.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the last null check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId` (diff: `AccessTokenContext.java`). This means `rawTokenId` is never validated and a caller can construct `AccessTokenContext` with `rawTokenId == null` without failing fast. Later, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, which would produce a token id suffix of the literal string `null` if that happens. The constructor guard is therefore incorrect and represents a real correctness defect introduced by this diff, even though current in-diff call sites pass non-null ids.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The lazy refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut insert into grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts without any duplicate-shortcut check, bypassing the collision validation that postInit enforces, so a grant registered after startup with a shortcut colliding with an existing grant silently overwrites the shortcut-to-grant mapping. In exactly the scenario these methods were written for (the code comment 'Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed'), tokens issued before the redeploy decode via getTokenContextFromTokenId to the wrong grant type with no error raised, feeding misclassified token context to any consumer of the new SPI.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() there is a one-time collision check based on grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts size equality, but the lazy refresh paths bypass it. Specifically, getShortcutByGrantType() does `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` and `grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut)` with no duplicate-shortcut/duplicate-id validation. If a newly deployed OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returns a shortcut already used by an existing grant, this overwrites the existing shortcut->grant mapping. Then getTokenContextFromTokenId() resolves the 2-char grant shortcut via factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut(), which will now return the wrong grant type without error. This is a real correctness issue grounded in the diff and matches the intended dynamic-refresh scenario mentioned in the comments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId is doubly broken — it reads the wrong window (items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6), mixing the last char of tokenType with the first char of grantType) and inverts the comparison (returns false when the window EQUALS the expected shortcut) — so it matches any '<6-char-context>:<uuid>' token ID regardless of which grant shortcut was encoded. expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh and expectAuthReqIdToToken pass for any grant: a refresh token whose Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute is dropped (encoding 'na') or a code-to-token response encoding 'cc' still matches, so the only integration-level verification of this PR's grant-encoding feature checks nothing beyond 'one colon plus UUID tail', and regressions in TokenManager.validateToken's refresh wiring or any grant's setAttribute call stay green.
matched_golden_ids: In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags the same two bugs in isAccessTokenId as the golden comment: it uses the wrong substring window for the grant shortcut (should be substring(4,6)) and the equality logic is inverted (it returns false on a matching shortcut instead of true, combined with UUID check).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] testIncorrectGrantType passes by catching a NullPointerException thrown from the null sessionFactory inside DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut's refresh fallback (before() never calls postInit, so sessionFactory is null and 'ac' is absent from the hand-built map), never reaching the IllegalArgumentException('Unknown value ... for grant type') branch the test claims to verify. The unknown-grant-shortcut validation in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId has zero real coverage: because the catch is the broad 'catch (RuntimeException)', deleting the IllegalArgumentException throw entirely leaves this test green, so malformed grant shortcuts in token IDs are unguarded by the suite.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before()` never calls `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(...)`, so `sessionFactory` remains null. In `testIncorrectGrantType`, the token id uses grant shortcut `ac` which is not added to the hand-built `grantsByShortcuts` map. Therefore `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac")` falls into its refresh fallback and dereferences `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)`, which would throw a `NullPointerException` (a `RuntimeException`) before `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` can throw the intended `IllegalArgumentException` for unknown grant shortcuts. Since the test catches any `RuntimeException`, it would still pass even if the specific unknown-grant validation/exception were removed, so the finding correctly identifies a test-coverage/validation assertion weakness rather than a runtime defect in production (where `postInit` sets `sessionFactory`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the method TokenManager.initToken calls to derive every issued access-token ID — is never invoked by any test in this diff (checked DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java, whose five methods only exercise getTokenContextFromTokenId/encodeTokenId string round-trips, and AssertEvents.java, whose isAccessTokenId matcher checks only shape). The TRANSIENT/OFFLINE/ONLINE derivation and the lightweight-token detection are unverified: inverting userSession.isOffline() or the persistence-state comparison puts a wrong 'on'/'of'/'tr' prefix on every token issued by the realm and every test in this diff stays green.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial logic in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() (deriving SessionType from userSession persistence/offline state, and TokenType from AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)), and TokenManager.initToken() now depends on it to generate every access-token ID. However, the only added unit test (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest) exercises getTokenContextFromTokenId()/encodeTokenId() round-trips and never calls getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(), and the AssertEvents change only validates token-id shape/pattern rather than the derivation logic. So the new context-derivation branch behavior is not directly covered by tests in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] before() hand-populates the package-private grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts maps with two synthetic entries and never calls factory.postInit, so postInit's provider-registry wiring and its duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException guard are executed by no test. A swapped put() in postInit or a broken duplicate-shortcut guard fails no unit test, and none of the real factory shortcuts ('ac','cc','pg','pc','rt','te','ci','dg','ro') is ever asserted against a real factory — two grants shipping the same shortcut would silently overwrite grantsByShortcuts and corrupt token-ID decoding with the suite green until the untested startup check fires.

adjudication.rationale: The new unit test DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before() constructs DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, calls init(null), then directly assigns and populates the package-private fields grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts with only two real grant mappings plus UNKNOWN, and never calls factory.postInit(...). Therefore none of the real postInit logic in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory (loading OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations via sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream, building shortcut maps from getShortcut(), and the duplicate-shortcut/ID guard that throws IllegalStateException when map sizes differ) is exercised by any test shown in the diff. As a result, regressions in postInit wiring or the duplicate-shortcut protection could go undetected by this unit test suite even though they are nontrivial logic introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The decode-side validation branches — the encodedContext.length() != 6 guard and the unknown session-type and token-type shortcut guards — are triggered by no test in the diff (all five test methods feed valid 6-char contexts or the colon-less '1234'). Removing the length guard makes a malformed ID like 'onrtacc:uuid' silently decode with a shifted parse (st='on', tt='rt', gt='ac') instead of throwing, and no test fails; the only negative-path test (testIncorrectGrantType) targets the grant guard and passes via NPE, so none of these three guards has any coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial decode-side validation in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId()` (the `encodedContext.length() != 6` check and the unknown sessionType/tokenType shortcut checks), but the added tests only cover (a) valid 6-char contexts and (b) the colon-less legacy case. There is no test that supplies a malformed context length (e.g., 7 chars) or an unknown session/token-type shortcut to prove those guards work. The finding’s detail that `testIncorrectGrantType` “passes via NPE” is inaccurate (it would throw an `IllegalArgumentException` from the grant-type guard), but the core point—no coverage for the length/session/token-type guards—is grounded in the diff and is a concrete test gap rather than a demonstrated functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] encodeTokenId's UNKNOWN-tokenType guard and unknown-grantType guard are never executed: testOldToken's context trips the sessionType guard first (line 101) and every other test encodes known values, so lines 104-106 and 108-111 have zero coverage. Deleting either guard fails no test; an UNKNOWN-tokenType context would then encode as a 'un'-prefixed ID that round-trips back as UNKNOWN without error, silently changing the reject-unknown contract with no suite coverage.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(), there are three reject-unknown guards: sessionType UNKNOWN (lines ~100-102), tokenType UNKNOWN (lines ~103-106), and unknown grantType via null shortcut (lines ~108-111). The added tests only exercise the sessionType UNKNOWN guard via testOldToken() (ctx has both sessionType UNKNOWN and tokenType UNKNOWN, so the sessionType guard throws first), and all other tests encode contexts with known tokenType and a grantType that is mapped (including the "na" UNKNOWN value being explicitly mapped in the test factory), so the tokenType-UNKNOWN and null-grant-shortcut branches are indeed not covered by this diff’s tests. That’s a concrete test-coverage gap around the intended reject-unknown contract, not a demonstrated functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The GRANT_TYPE attribute wiring added here and at the grant-specific sites (ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient) has no asserting coverage in this diff's test changes, which reference only the ac/dg/rt/ci shortcuts through the vacuous isAccessTokenId matcher. If createTokenResponse's setAttribute is dropped or a factory's shortcut is mis-registered, client-credentials, password, token-exchange and pre-authorized-code tokens encode 'na' or a wrong shortcut and every test in the diff stays green — the round-trip unit tests use synthetic map entries, not the real factories' shortcuts, so no test ties these grants' wiring to an issued jti.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds new GRANT_TYPE propagation into ClientSessionContext (e.g., OAuth2GrantType.Context.grantType from form param; OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE; additional setAttribute calls in ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, StandardTokenExchangeProvider, TokenManager refresh), and then encodes it into the access token `jti` via TokenContextEncoderProvider. The accompanying test changes don’t actually assert the grant shortcut in issued `jti`s: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId() is effectively non-asserting for the grant shortcut (it checks `items[0].substring(3, 5)` and returns false when it equals the expected shortcut, so it will pass even when the encoded grant shortcut is wrong). Also, the unit test DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest uses synthetic grant-shortcut maps rather than the real registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory shortcuts, so it doesn’t validate wiring/registration. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap/incorrect matcher rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new isAccessTokenId matcher never validates the grant shortcut: it slices items[0].substring(3, 5) — the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant shortcut — instead of the grant shortcut at substring(4, 6), and its early-return condition is inverted (it returns false when the slice EQUALS the expected shortcut), so the grant check is dead code. The matcher accepts any '<prefix>:<uuid>' token ID regardless of which grant/session/token type was encoded, so the four updated assertions (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) are vacuous — a regression encoding the wrong grant shortcut in every access-token ID passes the integration suite undetected.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the grant shortcut check is implemented as `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, which (a) slices the wrong range for a 6-char context prefix (grant shortcut should be at indices 4..6, not 3..5), and (b) has the logic inverted (it fails when the slice *equals* the expected shortcut, and otherwise proceeds). As a result, the matcher effectively only enforces the `:<uuid>` part (`isUUID().matches(items[1])`) and does not validate the expected grant shortcut, making the updated assertions in expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken vacuous.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The AccessTokenContext constructor null-checks grantType twice — the guard labeled "Null rawTokenId not allowed" also calls requireNonNull(grantType, ...), so rawTokenId is never validated despite the message. A caller passing a null rawTokenId (an extension implementing TokenContextEncoderProvider, or a decode-then-re-encode path) does not fail fast but silently produces a token ID containing the literal string 'null' (e.g. 'onrtna:null'), corrupting the jti of every token issued through that path.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the null-check intended for `rawTokenId` is wrong: it calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId` (see `AccessTokenContext.java`). Therefore `rawTokenId` can be null without failing fast. This is observable because `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, which would yield the literal string `"null"` if `rawTokenId` is null, producing an invalid/corrupted token id format.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The getShortcut() javadoc documents a "3-letters shortcut" while DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-requires the encoded prefix to be exactly 6 characters (a 2-char grant shortcut), and neither encodeTokenId nor the factory's postInit validates shortcut length. A third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory following the documented contract (e.g. returning "uma") gets tokens encoded as 'onrtuma:<uuid>' without any error, and the framework's own decoder then throws IllegalArgumentException("Expected length of 6") for every such token — the encoder issues token IDs its own decoder rejects, and nothing flags the violation at startup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an encoding/decoding contract mismatch for grant type shortcuts. `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory#getShortcut()` Javadoc says it is “usually like 3-letters shortcut”, but `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` blindly concatenates `sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grantShort(+':'+rawId)` without validating `grantShort` length, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId()` hard-requires the pre-':' context to be exactly 6 chars (`if (encodedContext.length() != 6) throw ... Expected length of 6.`), implying a 2-char grant shortcut. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` validates only uniqueness (map sizes), not shortcut length. Therefore, a provider following the documented (3-letter) shortcut can produce token IDs the built-in decoder rejects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] postInit calls the newly added getShortcut() on every registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory at boot and throws IllegalStateException on any shortcut collision, turning per-request grant behavior into a hard startup dependency. A deployment running a custom grant extension compiled against the pre-upgrade interface (no getShortcut method) fails Keycloak startup with AbstractMethodError during postInit, and a recompiled custom grant whose shortcut collides with a built-in ('cc', 'rt', ...) or with the reserved 'na' fails startup via the map-size IllegalStateException — both are boot failures with no config bypass, blocking upgrade and mixed-version rolling restarts for anyone using custom grants.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` unconditionally iterates all `OAuth2GrantType` provider factories and calls `gtf.getShortcut()` at boot. In Java this interface change is binary-incompatible: any custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation compiled against the old interface (without `getShortcut`) will throw `AbstractMethodError` when `postInit()` invokes it, preventing startup. Additionally, `postInit()` enforces uniqueness via a size-equality check after populating `grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts`; any shortcut collision (including collision with the reserved `UNKNOWN = "na"` which is forcibly inserted) triggers an `IllegalStateException` during boot. Both failure modes are hard startup dependencies introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] postInit puts the factory-returned shortcut straight into ConcurrentHashMap (grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName)) with no null or format validation of the new extension point. A grant factory whose getShortcut() returns null crashes Keycloak startup with a bare NullPointerException from ConcurrentHashMap.put (null key/value forbidden), with no message identifying which factory produced the null — the operator gets an undiagnosable boot failure instead of a validation error.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit, the new extension point OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is consumed without validation: `String grantShortcut = gtf.getShortcut(); grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName);` (and similarly for grantsToShortcuts). Because these are ConcurrentHashMaps (which reject null keys/values), any grant factory returning null (or possibly null id) will trigger a startup-time NullPointerException from the map put, with no explicit error identifying the offending factory. The diff introduces this new method and the unguarded registration logic, so the crash path is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] initToken unconditionally replaces the UUID access-token jti with the encoded 'xxxyyyzz:<uuid>' form for every newly issued token, with no feature flag, dual-format period, or migration note for this externally consumed identifier (the jti claim and the Details.TOKEN_ID event detail). At the moment of rollout, OIDC resource servers and audit/ETL pipelines that store jti in UUID-typed columns or parse Details.TOKEN_ID as a UUID (a decade-long Keycloak invariant) start rejecting every new token with no way to disable the encoding short of rollback, and a rollback leaves both jti formats in flight until existing tokens expire.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TokenManager.initToken(...)` no longer sets `token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())` directly, but instead always encodes it via `TokenContextEncoderProvider` (`token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx))`), producing IDs of the form `ssssss:<rawId>` (e.g., `onrtcc:<uuid>`). This is unconditional in the new code path (no feature flag/opt-out or transitional dual-format logic in the diff) and tests were updated to expect non-UUID `Details.TOKEN_ID` values. That makes the finding’s backward-compatibility concern about externally consumed `jti` / event token IDs diff-grounded, but it’s not a verifiable correctness defect by itself (it may be an intended breaking change).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId's grant-type check is dead code: it slices the wrong characters (items[0].substring(3, 5) grabs token-type-char + first grant-char instead of the grant shortcut at substring(4, 6)) and inverts the comparison (returns false when the slice EQUALS the expected shortcut), so the grant verification never rejects anything. For any well-formed encoded token ID (e.g. 'onrtac:<uuid>' checked against 'ac'), substring(3,5) yields 'ta', the equality is false, and the matcher falls through to the UUID check and passes — so expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh and expectAuthReqIdToToken all pass regardless of which grant shortcut was actually encoded; a token mislabeled 'na' (or with any wrong grant) sails through the suite, leaving the PR's only integration-level verification of the new token-ID format verifying nothing.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(), the grant shortcut is extracted incorrectly and the comparison is inverted. The encoded token context is 6 chars (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grantShortcut) as produced by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(). Therefore the grant shortcut is at substring(4,6), but the matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which grabs the last char of tokenType plus the first char of grant. Additionally, it returns false when the slice equals expectedGrantShortcut (should reject when it does NOT equal). As written, for a valid token like "onrtac:<uuid>" and expected "ac", substring(3,5) yields "ta", equality is false, and the matcher falls through to UUID-only validation, so the grant shortcut is effectively not verified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The AccessTokenContext constructor's fourth guard, Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"), re-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId, so the null-rawTokenId validation the message promises never fires. A null rawTokenId is silently accepted by the constructor, and encodeTokenId then emits a token ID ending in the literal string 'null' (e.g. 'onrtac:null') as the jti of an issued access token instead of failing fast with the intended exception — any caller (the framework's own future call sites or a custom TokenContextEncoderProvider) passing a null id gets malformed token IDs with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the fourth null-guard is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId` (see `AccessTokenContext.java`). This means `rawTokenId` can be passed as null without triggering the intended validation. In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId`, the token id is built via string concatenation `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, which would yield the literal suffix `":null"` if `rawTokenId` is null. While current call sites in this diff pass a generated id, the constructor bug is real and verifiable from the diff and can produce malformed encoded token IDs if any caller supplies null.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] postInit unconditionally calls gtf.getShortcut() on every registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory, but getShortcut() is a newly added abstract method on the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI, so grant factories compiled against the previous interface have no implementation of it. A deployment carrying a pre-compiled custom grant-type extension (a providers/ JAR built against the old server-spi-private interface) throws AbstractMethodError inside DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit at boot, and Keycloak fails to start entirely after upgrade — a hard startup crash with no error message pointing at the missing getShortcut() implementation, where the same extension worked before this change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (server-spi-private) without a default implementation. In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`, it unconditionally casts each factory to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` and calls `gtf.getShortcut()`. In Java, adding an abstract method to an interface is binary-incompatible: a custom grant factory class compiled against the previous interface version will load but will not have an implementation for the new method, so invoking it will throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime during boot. This matches the described startup crash path grounded in `postInit`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The startup validation block only checks shortcut uniqueness (map-size comparison) and never validates shortcut length, while getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-rejects any encoded prefix whose context part is not exactly 6 characters — and the new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory javadoc actively tells implementors a shortcut is 'usually like 3-letters'. A custom grant returning a 3-character shortcut (following the SPI javadoc) passes the postInit validation cleanly, its tokens are issued today by the production encode path with 7-character prefixes, and every subsequent getTokenContextFromTokenId call on those tokens throws IllegalArgumentException("Expected length of 6") — undecodable tokens already in the field, discovered only after a follow-up PR wires decoding in.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hard-codes the token-id context prefix to exactly 6 characters in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` (`if (encodedContext.length() != 6) throw ... "Expected length of 6."`), implicitly requiring a 2-char grant shortcut (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grantType). However, `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` is newly introduced with Javadoc saying it is “usually like 3-letters”, and neither `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` nor `encodeTokenId` validates shortcut length. `encodeTokenId` will happily concatenate a longer shortcut, producing a non-6 context part, which then becomes undecodable by `getTokenContextFromTokenId`. This is a real incompatibility/contract bug introduced by the change.
